Which cuts are un-cuttable mortises (cookie re-scope, instance identity) that must be dry-fit and proven square before the pegs are driven? Does the datum have to be the fair public face at all, or can the hidden auth/infra edge be the datum while a different name is the show face? And is the frame light enough (2 users) to rear the irreversible joints now, before it gets heavy?
distance_rationale: Raising a load-bearing timber frame by the scribe rule is a pre-industrial physical craft with no lineage to software, branding, DNS, cartography, or hydrology, yet it isolates the ONE structural act the other five lenses circle but never own: the moment a builder commits a reference DATUM. In scribe-rule framing every timber is marked from a chosen 'face side / face edge'; that datum is picked once on the flat framing floor, and every mortise, tenon, and brace is scribed relative to it. Once chosen it is silent and load-bearing — you never see it again, but the whole frame's squareness inherits it. A mortise cannot be un-cut; the cheapest moment to move anything is on the layout floor before the timbers are reared, and after the raising the joints carry static load unchanged for centuries. This is orthogonal to harbor engineering (which owns FLOW and sequencing THROUGH a channel and the risk of stranding a moving fleet) because carpentry owns a STATIC committed geometry and the risk of a racking, un-cuttable joint; and orthogonal to cartography (which owns the NAME engraved) because the carpenter is wholly indifferent to what the building is called and owns only whether it stands plumb and square. The isomorph to the target: which domain becomes the load-bearing reference datum (the Clerk primary-domain / cookie-scope / OAuth origin that every app is silently scribed from) is chosen ONCE, at near-zero cost today, and every later hull inherits it — and the target document treats this as a name contest rather than a datum-commitment decision.
expected_isomorphisms: The face side / face edge (the single reference datum every timber is scribed from) = the registrable domain that becomes the load-bearing reference — the Clerk primary domain, the .cookie-scope, the OAuth origin — that every hull is silently marked from; it is chosen once and never re-seen, but the whole ecosystem's squareness inherits it.

Laying out the whole frame on the flat framing floor before any joint is cut = specifying the full URL architecture and datum choice at ~2 users, on the ground, before any hull is 'reared' into consumer-facing load — the near-zero-cost layout window the ledger keeps gesturing at.

A mortise-and-tenon joint cannot be un-cut; a mis-scribed mortise means a scrapped timber or a shimmed, racking frame = the cookie-domain re-scope / Clerk instance identity that atomically logs everyone out and cannot be quietly reversed once real load is on it.

Reference datum need not equal the show face: the datum the frame is squared from is often a hidden interior edge, not the fair face the public sees = jawncloud.com can remain the hidden load-bearing auth/infra datum while jawnverse.com is the fair public face — the split-harbor 'third option', reframed as datum-vs-fairface rather than as a name contest.

Racking (a frame going out of square because members were scribed off inconsistent references) = each hull authenticating/cookie-ing off a different implicit datum, so the ecosystem cannot be squared later without pulling joints apart.

Raising the frame with too few hands vs. waiting for a full raising crew = doing the irreversible datum commitment now while the frame is light (2 users) vs. after it is heavy — the timber does not get lighter by waiting.
A test-assembled bent knocked down and re-reared = the reversible-until-a-named-step migration sequence: dry-fit and prove square on the floor before driving the pegs that make it permanent.
focus: Whether the decision commits a single coherent load-bearing reference DATUM that every current and future hull is scribed from — and whether that datum is chosen deliberately at today's near-zero-cost layout stage rather than defaulted-into by whichever hull happened to be reared first. name: fd-timberframe-scribe-datum-commitment
persona: Apply the perspective of a master timber-frame carpenter working by the scribe rule: someone who, before cutting a single joint, lays the whole frame out flat on the framing floor and chooses the one reference face and edge every timber will be marked from; who knows a mortise once cut cannot be un-cut and that a frame scribed off inconsistent references will rack and never come square; who distinguishes the hidden datum the frame is squared from from the fair face the public will see; who dry-fits and knocks down a bent to prove it square before driving the pegs that make it permanent; and who knows the cheapest moment to move anything is on the flat floor before the timbers are reared, because the timber never gets lighter by waiting.
review_areas: Datum identity: name the single load-bearing reference the whole ecosystem is (or should be) scribed from — the Clerk primary domain / cookie scope / OAuth origin — and flag that the target frames this as a NAME contest (jawnverse vs jawncloud) rather than a datum-commitment decision; the highest-value finding is that the doc never asks 'which domain is the reference face every hull inherits'.

Layout-before-cut discipline: whether the full URL/hull architecture is laid out flat and committed now, at ~2 users, before hulls are reared into consumer load — or whether hulls (jawnfit already 301'd, log/stats live) are being reared one at a time off an unstated datum, guaranteeing a rack.

Un-cuttable joints: enumerate which migration steps are mortises that cannot be un-cut (cookie-domain re-scope that atomically logs everyone out, Clerk instance identity change, OAuth origin re-pin) versus reversible dry-fit steps, and require they be proven square on the floor before the pegs are driven.

Datum vs. fair face (the split option, reframed): assess the third option as a carpentry fact — the datum the frame is squared from need not be the fair face the public sees, so jawncloud.com can stay the hidden load-bearing auth datum while jawnverse.com is the show face; flag that the target treats 'Clerk primary domain' and 'consumer apex' as necessarily the same timber when the craft says they need not be.

Racking risk across hulls: whether five-plus sibling hulls (jawnfit, jawnbase, jawntrack, jawnlog, JawnScope) are each being scribed off a consistent datum, or whether inconsistent references across hulls will put the ecosystem out of square in a way that cannot be trued up later without pulling joints apart.

Weight-of-the-frame timing: whether the irreversible datum commitment is being made now while the frame is light (2 users) or deferred until it is heavy; the timber does not get lighter by waiting, so a deferred commitment with no named raising day is itself a defect.
severity_examples: P0: The recommendation rears jawnverse.com as the consumer face while every hull is still silently scribed from the .jawncloud.com datum (cookie scope, Clerk primary, OAuth origin) with no decision about which is THE reference face — the frame is being raised off two inconsistent datums and will rack at the first hull that authenticates, un-squarable without pulling the auth joints apart.

P1: The plan drives the un-cuttable joints (cookie-domain re-scope / Clerk instance identity) without a dry-fit-and-prove-square step, so a mis-scribed cut cannot be un-cut and the frame is scrapped or permanently shimmed rather than knocked down and re-reared.

P1: The datum commitment is deferred with no named raising day while the frame is still light (2 users), so it will be cut when the frame is heavy and every joint bears live load — the target names the 2-user fact but never sets the raising-day trigger.

P2: The datum-vs-fair-face distinction is never drawn, so the doc assumes the reference the frame is squared from (Clerk primary/cookie datum) must be the same timber as the show face the public types, foreclosing the cheaper hidden-datum design.
source_domain: Traditional timber-frame carpentry by the scribe rule (master-builder joinery: choosing the single reference face/edge every timber is scribed from, laying out the sill and ridge on the framing floor, cutting irreversible mortise-and-tenon joints, and raising a frame whose whole geometry is committed at layout and bears static load unchanged for centuries)
